query: What recurring issues drive resolution inefficiency?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents from short_description gives a clean axis to group recurring issues (printer dominates). Values align well with source text.

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: A distinct failure-mode axis useful for spotting inefficiency drivers. Mostly well-grounded, though 'database connection lost' -> connectivity_failure is a reasonable reading; somewhat correlated with incident_category but adds a different lens.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to resolution efficiency. However short_descriptions rarely state the action taken; values like 'repair'/'network_fix' are often inferred defaults from category rather than grounded, so some assertions exceed what the text supports.

per_column.name: reassignment_indicator
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is a strong signal of resolution inefficiency, so highly relevant. But the sampled source text (short_description + timestamps) contains no reassignment history; True/False values appear unsupported by available fields.

per_column.name: self_resolution_indicator
per_column.rationale: Self-resolution vs assisted is a useful efficiency dimension, but nothing in the sampled source text indicates self-resolution; e.g. connectivity loss marked self_resolution=True is not warranted. Values seem invented.

per_column.name: resolver_agent
per_column.rationale: Agent-level comparison is relevant to efficiency, but this largely duplicates the existing assigned_to/closed_by columns. Values are names not present in the sampled source text, so groundedness is uncertain and possibly a restatement.

per_column.name: scope_breadth
per_column.rationale: Blast-radius axis is a genuinely new grouping dimension for inefficiency. Some values are warranted ('floor 3' -> location_wide), but others like generic 'printer not working' -> shared_office_equipment and 'database' -> infrastructure_wide are inferred beyond what the text states.

per_column.name: affected_asset_class
per_column.rationale: Well-grounded extraction of the asset from short_description, but heavily overlaps incident_category, reducing incremental analytical leverage.

judge.rationale: The set provides several genuinely useful axes for diagnosing resolution inefficiency (category, failure_type, scope_breadth, reassignment). Groundedness is mixed: extraction-style columns (incident_category, affected_asset_class) read soundly from short_description, but the process/behavioral columns (reassignment, self_resolution, resolution_action_type) assert facts the sampled source text does not support and appear inferred or invented. resolver_agent and affected_asset_class also partly restate existing/other columns.
